old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a scientific experiment setup on a metallic surface. At the center of the frame is a rectangular glass plate with a square cutout, through which a bright light source is visible. The light creates a vivid display of colors, including shades of purple, blue, green, yellow, and orange, forming concentric rings around the light source. To the right of the glass plate, there is a black mechanical device with a circular opening, possibly a lens or a filter holder, mounted on a stand. The background features a dark, textured wall, and part of another metallic object is visible on the left side of the frame. The scene remains static throughout the video, focusing on the interaction between the light source and the glass plate, highlighting the dispersion of light into its constituent colors. There are no characters or animals present, and the camera maintains a steady position, emphasizing the detailed patterns created by the light.

caption: The video captures a fixed optical-bench view in which a transparent rectangular plate stands upright on a black perforated table, its left edge gripped by a metal clamp engraved with vertical text. A circular pool of warm light falls across the plate, and within that halo a sharp square region displays curved rainbow bands of purple, magenta, orange, and yellow, while a bright reflection glows along the left rim. To the right, a black optical mount sits on a translation stage with an adjustment knob and a white-and-silver micrometer handle, and a horizontal metal rod passes behind it against a dark background board. Throughout the excerpt the plate, clamp, mount, rod, and square outline hold their positions, showing no object translation or camera motion. The colored bands inside the square, however, undergo a very slight, gradual reshaping, their curves and widths drifting almost imperceptibly over time. The luminous halo and its left-edge reflection likewise fluctuate subtly in intensity. The patterned square is present throughout, so the slow fringe drift continues without a visible onset or completion.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness

Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
